neighbours.label: preposition right after a send / mail / deliver verb or noun (sent with, mailed with, letter from), other than ' to'
fire: Your tickets will be mailed with a printed copy of the schedule next week.
The spammers send messages from hacked accounts so they look trustworthy.
Please return the signed form, which was sent with your welcome packet.
Grandma always ships parcels from the little post office on Main Street.
The courier delivered the package on Sunday morning, which surprised us.
We received a postcard from Lisbon, sent from a hotel near the harbour.
Invoices are emailed with a link to the payment portal at the end of each month.
The note he posted with the cheque explained why the payment was late.
quiet: Your tickets will be printed with a copy of the schedule next week.
The spammers write messages in broken English so they look suspicious.
Please return the signed form, which was filled in with blue ink.
Grandma always buys bread from the little bakery on Main Street.
The courier rested at home on Sunday morning, which surprised us.
We drank coffee in Lisbon, sitting in a cafe near the harbour.
Invoices are paid with a credit card at the end of each month.
